The widening confidence intervals across the horizons directly reflected the increasing uncertainty inherent in forecasting further into the future. Conversely, a severe economic downturn, a sudden and significant policy error by central banks or governments, the escalation of a global conflict, or a systemic financial shock could cause the value to drop considerably below the lower bounds of the intervals. These types of high-impact events represent tail risks that are difficult to quantify within standard probabilistic models but nonetheless have the potential to drastically alter market trajectories.
